intended_object: Given a ring homomorphism f : R → S whose image consists of pairwise commuting elements, the induced ring homomorphism Rᵐᵒᵖ → S, x ↦ f(unop x). Inferred from the docstring and from the parallel construction MonoidHom.fromOpposite.
explanation:
The definition sets the map to `f ∘ unop`. It takes the additive structure from f composed with the additive equivalence `opAddEquiv.symm`. It takes the multiplicative structure from `MonoidHom.fromOpposite`, which uses the commutation hypothesis to get f(unop(x·y)) = f(unop y · unop x) = f(unop y) f(unop x) = f(unop x) f(unop y). This is exactly the ring homomorphism Rᵐᵒᵖ →+* S described in the docstring.

The commutation hypothesis is the condition that makes the map multiplicative. It is not a restriction beyond what the construction needs.

The `Semiring` assumptions match the companion `RingHom.toOpposite` in the same file. In principle `NonAssocSemiring` would be enough, since `MonoidHom.fromOpposite` only needs `MulOneClass`. That is a minor typeclass detail and not a substantive loss of generality, so I do not count it as too narrow.

This is itself the Mathlib declaration, and Mathlib has no other declaration defining the same object.
